fields.Participants: Regional Ops Mgr, Store Manager, Merch Coord

Automation Opportunity: - Inspection findings with photos auto-routed to the Store Manager's worklist with the 48-hour SLA; finding-closure auto-verified on the next cycle
Controls: - CTL-195: display integrity — a display that misrepresents product is a consumer-protection risk per W2682; operational: Regional Ops Manager finding-closure sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inspection-decoupled-from-action risk**: the inspection generates findings but the Store Manager doesn't remediate within 48 hours; mitigated by the finding-age tracker and Regional Ops Manager follow-up on open findings >48 hours

- **Rubric-drift risk**: different inspectors score the same display differently (subjectivity); mitigated by the photo-evidence requirement per finding and the rubric calibration sessions for the Regional Ops team
System Touchpoints: - Planogram/audit (links to VS-55 / W86 planogram compliance audit, VS-177 field-retail-standards audit) — the inspection rubric and scoring
- Sample inventory (links to VS-62 / W2337) — completeness check against the sample-presence threshold
- Field-audit tooling (links to VS-133 / VS-177) — the mobile inspection app the Regional Ops Mgr uses
Time Estimate: ~2.5 hours/store inspection × 200 stores + ~3 hours remediation per store = **~700–900 hours/month** Regional Ops + Store Managers (Regional Ops Managers cover ~40 stores each).

steps.activity: Regional Ops Manager (or designated field auditor) inspects the sample displays across ~8 zones per store: condition, cleanliness, completeness (samples present vs. the W2337 minimum threshold), pricing-label accuracy (links to W2345), visual-merchandising standard adherence (links to VS-55 planogram); scores each zone on a standard rubric

Store Manager remediates the findings within 48 hours; damaged samples replaced from the store reserve or ordered from the DC (W2343); persistent issues escalated to the Merchandising Coordinator for a program-level fix

fields.Participants: Dept Supervisor, Merch Coordinator, DC Ops
fields.Trigger: Store reports damaged or missing sample

Automation Opportunity: - Below-threshold auto-approval for low-value replacements; damage-frequency dashboard auto-aggregated for the W2348 review
Controls: - CTL-416 (ensure controlled execution — Display Maintenance & Sample Refresh (PA-62.2).)
- operational: sample-SKU transaction integrity; operational: photo-evidence requirement per damage report
Pain Points / Risks: - **Replacement-latency risk**: the 3–5 day delivery window leaves the display incomplete, losing conversion; mitigated by the store reserve stock (a small on-hand buffer of high-damage samples) for immediate swap

- **Damage-pattern blindness risk**: the same sample (e.g., a fragile laminate chip) damages repeatedly across stores but the pattern isn't seen because each replacement is handled as a one-off; mitigated by the W2348 quarterly analytics aggregating damage frequency per sample-SKU to flag a durability redesign
System Touchpoints: - Inventory/replenishment (links to VS-62 / W2337, VS-05 / W6) — the sample-SKU replenishment
- DC distribution (links to VS-04 / W3) — replacement rides the next regular delivery
- Disposition (links to VS-05 / W91 damaged-goods, VS-73 waste) — the damaged sample's disposition (return-to-vendor, recycle, dispose)
Time Estimate: ~10 min/report × ~650 replacements/month + DC handling absorbed = **~150–200 hours/month** Dept Supervisors (distributed across stores).

steps.activity: Supervisor reports the damaged sample in the system: sample-ID, damage type, photo evidence; system generates the replacement order; Merch Coordinator approves (or auto-approved if below threshold); replacement shipped with the next DC delivery

Automation Opportunity: - Cleaning-task auto-scheduled in the VS-07 weekly checklist; completion auto-tracked via the task system
Controls: - CTL-416 (ensure controlled execution — Display Maintenance & Sample Refresh (PA-62.2).)
- Operational: Department Supervisor weekly sign-off on the cleaning checklist
Pain Points / Risks: - **Skip-risk**: the weekly clean is skipped during busy periods, and the display degrades (dusty samples depress conversion); mitigated by the task in the VS-07 weekly checklist with Department Supervisor sign-off
- **Cleaning-product-damage risk**: the wrong cleaner damages a sample (abrasive on a polished stone, solvent on a laminate); mitigated by the per-material cleaning spec in the task instructions
System Touchpoints: - Store daily-ops (links to VS-07 / W5 daily store operations, W47 maintenance) — the cleaning task in the weekly store-ops cycle
- Planogram (links to VS-55) — the sample-order organization standard
Time Estimate: ~30–45 min/week/store × 200 stores ≈ ~6,000–9,000 min ≈ **~100–150 hours/week ≈ ~5,200–7,800 hours/year** Store Staff (absorbed into the store-ops routine, not incremental headcount).

steps.activity: Designated staff cleans the sample displays weekly: dust tile boards, wipe countertop chips, replace faded color cards, clean the display fixtures, organize the sample order; logs completion in the VS-07 daily-ops checklist

fields.Participants: Dept Supervisor, Pricing Analyst, Merch Coord
fields.Trigger: Price change or new sample added

Automation Opportunity: - Sample-label list auto-generated on every parent-SKU price change; label-refresh auto-verified on the W2342 inspection
Controls: - CTL-416 (ensure controlled execution — Display Maintenance & Sample Refresh (PA-62.2).)
- CTL-416 (price-tag accuracy — links to VS-08 / W69 price-compliance audit, DTI price-freeze compliance); operational: Department Supervisor label-application sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stale-price risk**: the sample shows the old price after an SRP change, misleading the customer and creating a DTI price-complaint exposure (links to W2682 consumer protection); mitigated by the auto-generated label list triggered by the parent price change

- **Mismatched-availability risk**: the sample displays a SKU that's discontinued or out of stock, frustrating the sample-to-order conversion; mitigated by the availability check on the label-refresh trigger
System Touchpoints: - Price-tag/labeling (links to VS-08 / W181 price-tag printing, VS-55 / W63 shelf-label generation) — the sample-label generation
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289 pricing master) — the SRP change that triggers the label refresh
- Item/sample master (links to VS-29 / W296) — the sample→parent link that flags the sample for re-labeling
Time Estimate: ~1.5 hours/month × 200 stores = **~300 hours/month ≈ ~3,600 hours/year** Dept Supervisors (absorbed into the store-ops pricing routine).

steps.activity: System generates the sample pricing labels when the parent SKU's SRP changes (the sample-SKU→parent-SKU link from W2334 surfaces the price-change impact); Supervisor prints and applies the labels to the sample display; ensures the sample SKU, product name, price, and order-availability match the current data

fields.Participants: IT Support, Store Manager, Digital PM

Automation Opportunity: - Device-health telemetry auto-ticketing (an offline device auto-opens an IT ticket without waiting for a store report)
Controls: - CTL-416 (ensure controlled execution — Display Maintenance & Sample Refresh (PA-62.2).)
- CTL-416 (IT-asset tracking — links to VS-99); operational: IT Support monthly maintenance log per device
Pain Points / Risks: - **Display-downtime risk**: a malfunctioning tablet sits broken for weeks because no one reports it (the store team assumes IT knows); mitigated by the device-health telemetry (MDM reports offline devices) and a "report a broken display" quick-path for Store staff
- **Theft/vandalism risk**: in-store tablets are theft targets and vandalism-prone; mitigated by the secure-mounting spec and the device-tracking (MDM locates/wipes a stolen device)
System Touchpoints: - IT asset/MDM (links to VS-27 / W48 helpdesk, W265 POS-terminal/peripheral management, VS-99 IT-asset lifecycle) — the tablet/kiosk as a managed device
- AR/catalog app (links to VS-62 / W2339, VS-75 digital engagement app) — the software under maintenance
- Network/connectivity (links to VS-27 / W366) — the in-store connectivity the displays depend on
Time Estimate: ~2.5 hours/store/month × 50 stores = **~125 hours/month ≈ ~1,500 hours/year** IT Support.

steps.activity: IT Support maintains the interactive sample displays: in-store tablets running the AR visualizer (W2339), digital kiosks with the product catalog; updates the software, replaces damaged tablets, troubleshoots connectivity (links to VS-27 IT ops)

fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Marketing, Vendor, Store Ops

Automation Opportunity: - Performance-vs-baseline dashboard auto-populated post-install; funding-term-expiry tracker
Controls: - CTL-39: co-op/rebate accuracy — the vendor funding validated; CTL-48 (rebate-dispute resolution if the vendor disputes the funding obligation); operational: VP Merchandising sign-off on any vendor display >PHP 500K fixture value
Pain Points / Risks: - **Clutter risk**: too many vendor-funded displays crowd the floor and dilute brand coherence; mitigated by the space-allocation gate in step 1 (a vendor display displaces standard merchandise, so the opportunity cost must be justified)

- **Funding-withdrawal risk**: the vendor funds the fixture year 1 then withdraws funding, leaving BuildRight with an orphan fixture; mitigated by the multi-year funding term in the agreement and a "funding ends → re-evaluate or decommission" clause
System Touchpoints: - Planogram/space (links to VS-55 / W314 planogram template, space-allocation) — the fixture's footprint allocated against the store's space plan
- Co-op/rebate (links to VS-39 / W27, VS-14 marketing co-op) — the vendor-funding terms recorded in the vendor agreement
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the performance-vs-baseline measurement
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/program × ~12 programs/year + ongoing performance monitoring absorbed = **~250–350 hours/year** Category Manager + Store Ops.

steps.activity: Vendor proposes a branded display (e.g., a Bosch power-tool wall, a Boysen paint station); Category Manager evaluates: brand alignment, customer experience, space requirement (against the VS-55 space-allocation plan), vendor funding level (is the vendor paying for the fixture and installation?)

Approved displays: vendor provides the fixture and installation; Store Ops coordinates the placement; Category Manager monitors the performance (traffic, conversion, sales lift) vs. the standard display baseline to validate the program

fields.Participants: Analytics Manager, Category Mgr, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - Performance dashboard auto-refreshed quarterly; bottom-performer auto-flagged for the Category Manager's review
Controls: - CTL-416 (ensure controlled execution — Display Maintenance & Sample Refresh (PA-62.2).)
- Operational: Analytics Manager methodology sign-off (attribution rules documented); Category Manager review of any display with conversion below threshold
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution-weakness risk**: sales-per-zone is hard to attribute cleanly (a customer may browse the tile display then buy at the counter, not at the display); mitigated by the W2340 sample-scan attribution as the cleaner signal where captured
- **Vanity-metric risk**: dwell time looks good but doesn't convert; mitigated by the conversion-rate (not dwell) as the primary KPI
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, W208 retail analytics) — the performance dataset
- Sample-to-order data (links to VS-62 / W2340) — the conversion-rate input
- Customer feedback (links to VS-13 / W65 CSAT/NPS) — the customer-experience input
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/quarter Analytics Manager = **~80–100 hours/year**, absorbed into the VS-28 analytics cadence.

steps.activity: Analytics Manager measures display performance: sales per display zone, sample-to-order conversion rate (from W2340), dwell time at displays (where sensor-equipped), customer feedback on displays; identifies the top- and bottom-performing displays and the damage-frequency patterns (from W2343)

fields.Trigger: Product delisted or display program ended

Automation Opportunity: - Decommission auto-triggered by the W68 product discontinuation; return-obligation auto-surfaced from the agreement master
Controls: - CTL-198: asset-grade display disposition; operational: Merch Coordinator decommission sign-off per program
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lingering-display risk**: the product is delisted but the display stays up, letting customers sample a product they can't buy; mitigated by the decommission triggered by the W68 discontinuation, not waiting for a manual catch
- **Asset-loss risk**: a vendor-owned display is scrapped instead of returned, forfeiting the deposit/credit; mitigated by the return-obligation check in step 1 against the W2347 agreement
System Touchpoints: - Item/sample master (links to VS-29 / W296, W68 discontinuation) — the sample-SKU status set to decommissioned
- Disposition (links to VS-05 / W91, VS-73 waste, W443 salvage/scrap) — the display-material disposition
- Vendor agreement (links to VS-39 / W27, VS-100 / W230) — the return obligation for vendor-funded displays
Time Estimate: ~1.5 weeks/decommission × ~75 decommissions/year + ~4 hours/store removal ≈ ~300 hours = **~200–400 hours/year** Merch Coordinator + Facilities + Store Managers.

steps.activity: Coordinator issues the decommission: remove the samples, dismantle the fixture, return the vendor-owned displays (per the W2347 agreement terms), dispose/recycle the BuildRight-owned materials (per VS-73 waste streams); restore the zone to the standard planogram
